headline: Stellar jumps 21% as Bitcoin holds flat despite record stock markets
summary: Bitcoin barely moved Friday, holding near its recent range despite record highs in equities and easing geopolitical tensions — a disconnect that CryptoQuant attributes to a shortage of new buyers even as long-term holders sit tight. The day's real action was in altcoins: Stellar surged 21.4% on renewed momentum, Hyperliquid climbed 9.2%, and XRP recovered above $1.30. Bitcoin Cash was the notable loser, sliding 7%.

winners.name: Stellar
winners.catalyst: Renewed market momentum drove Stellar sharply higher; no single specific announcement was identified as the trigger.

losers.name: Bitcoin Cash
losers.catalyst: Bitcoin Cash declined on no identified asset-specific catalyst; the move appears to reflect thin buying activity in lower-liquidity large-caps on a flat-volume day.

whyItMoved:
The headline story today isn't a big move — it's the absence of one. Bitcoin ended the day up just 0.3% even as US stock indices hit record highs, oil prices fell, and war-related tensions eased. Under normal conditions, that macro backdrop would be a tailwind for risk assets including crypto. The disconnect is explained, at least in part, by a CryptoQuant analysis published Friday: Bitcoin's supply is increasingly concentrated among long-term holders who aren't selling, but new buyers aren't stepping in to replace them. Record holder supply sounds bullish on the surface, but without fresh demand, it creates a ceiling rather than a floor. The Fear & Greed index sits at 23 — deep in Fear territory — which is consistent with a market where existing holders are patient but new capital is staying on the sidelines.

Amid that flat backdrop, altcoins found more movement. Stellar surged 21.4% with no clearly identified catalyst — the move appears to be momentum-driven. Hyperliquid climbed 9.2%, continuing a run that has made it one of the stronger performers in the top 15 this week. XRP recovered above $1.30 after a volume surge, though the weekly chart still shows sellers in control according to the CoinDesk report on the move. TRON was the notable decliner among the top 15, falling 3%.
worthKnowing: XRP climbed 2.4% after a volume surge pushed it back above $1.30, though the broader weekly trend still shows selling pressure outweighing buying.
OKX Ventures acquired a $53 million stake in South Korea's Coinone exchange, the latest sign of consolidation activity among major crypto trading platforms.

Prediction market platform Kalshi sued the state of Minnesota after the state passed a law criminalizing prediction markets — a case that could affect how crypto-adjacent prediction platforms operate in the US.
